text:
Priya: heads-up — saw a large spike from a partner test org that exhausted per-org burst tokens. Thinking through degrade strategies: failfast with 429, soft-queue with ETA headers + webhook callback, or return 503 to force fallback. Pros/cons?
Diego: can we do a small in-edge soft-queue (short lived token queue) that returns an ETA header instead of immediately rejecting? if we queue, need a clear surface for apps (headers + console).
Alex: caution — queuing keeps requests tied up and can inflate GPU occupancy. For sync UX, 429 is clean: client can backoff. For batch/async flows we should offer an explicit job API.
Maya: small clarif — currently when burst tokens are exhausted some routes return 503 from the edge to avoid backend overload. 503 tends to be treated as server error by clients; 429 signals rate limit. Behavioural difference matters for retries.
Sam: +1 on semantics. 429 with Retry-After is easier to reason about in billing/console. But if we want to preserve throughput we could accept and queue small bursts (soft-queue) for up to X seconds. Important: queueing must expose ETA and queue position.
InfraBot: :warning: alert triggered: per-org queue length > 500 (org: partner-test) — autoscaled queue spool created.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 — per-org burst saturation (link: https://incidents.re/redwood/INC-2026-0423)
Priya: UX ask for Console: visible queued_requests, p50/p99 wait times, ability for org admins to opt-in to "soft-queue" for bursts, and a per-key toggle. Suggest default: OFF for enterprise, ON as opt-in for dev orgs.
Diego: proposal sketch: introduce "soft-queue" policy middleware. Flow: precheck -> if tokens available go to fast path -> else if soft-queue enabled and queue_len < Q_limit accept into short queue and return 202 + headers -> else return 429 with reason=quota_exhausted. Implement queue at edge backed by lightweight FIFO, max wait 30s.
Alex: Implementation notes: add header signals so SDKs can detect this pattern. Suggested headers:
```http
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
X-Redwood-Queue-Id: q_abc123
X-Redwood-Queue-ETA: 12  # seconds
Retry-After: 12
```
If wait exceeds threshold we should evict and return 429 with body {error: 'queue_timeout'}.
Maya: Metrics required before rollout: queued_count, queue_wait_seconds (p50/p95/p99), queue_dropped_count, per-org queue_limit_exceeded. Dashboards + alerts: p50 > 2s or p99 > 10s should alert. Also capture whether request consumed burst token vs queued.
Priya: rollout plan: canary to 10% orgs next week behind a per-org config flag. Soft-queue default max wait = 30s, queue_limit = 100 per org, fallback -> 429. Need console toggle + API to opt in/out.
Diego: I'll draft RFC and add the middleware prototype. Need a short lifecycle: middleware + metrics + minimal console card (queued count + avg wait) for canary. Work items: 1) edge precheck + token-bucket integration, 2) queue store (in-memory at edge with eviction), 3) headers/webhook callback for async clients, 4) console opt-in toggle, 5) tests for overload scenarios.
Sam: small reminder — ensure traceability: logs should include trace_id + queue_id so we can link queued requests in traces and console. Also validate billing behavior: queued requests should only be billed on execution, not on enqueue.
Alex: agree. Also add a guide in devex on SDK behavior for queued responses and best-practice retry/backoff configs.
Maya: one more thought — circuit breaker: if queue_drop_rate spike > 5% for 5m, flip org into hard-fail (429) until manual reset. avoids cascading backend pressure.
Priya: perfect. Can we aim for RFC by EOD tomorrow? Diego will take lead. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Diego: will do — starting RFC now. planning deploy command for canary: `./scripts/deploy --canary soft-queue=10%`
InfraBot: deploy job queued: deploy/soft-queue -> canary 10% started by Diego.
Sam: great, ping me for console diff review.
